column1: # Shared tool registry — how to verify a tool, and how to install it, written
# once per tool rather than once per skill that needs it.
# runtime_tool_install_hint() from this file. Each skill's own requires.tsv says
# what it needs, under what condition, and how badly; this file says what to do
# about a tool that is missing.
#   kind       verify  the command that decides whether the tool is usable
#              default the instruction for a tool with no rows of its own
#   tool       tool id, or * for the fallback row of that kind
#   condition  <uname -s glob>:<uname -m glob> the row applies to; a bash case
#   group      hint rows sharing (tool, condition, group) are one first-match
#              chain: the first row whose probe resolves prints. Groups print in
#              ascending order, so a tool can emit an instruction, an
#   probe      command that must exist on PATH for the row to apply, or - for a
#              row that always applies and closes the chain
#   text       the line to print (hint, default) or the command to run (verify).
#              A default row's text carries one %s for the tool name.
# Line-oriented TSV and not JSON, deliberately: this table declares jq as a
# dependency, so a format needing jq to read it could not be read on the machine
# that is missing jq. awk and sed parse it.
# The verify column holds a command rather than a tool name so a tool that exists
# but is the wrong build can grow a functional probe here without a code change.
